_note: Add links to each category below. The IDEs category uses subgroups (Offline / Online) instead of a flat links array.

_link_schema.title: Display name of the link
_link_schema.description: One or two sentences describing the link and who it suits.
badges: one or more badge keys from _badges below

_badges.Student: Resource is suitable for student use
_badges.Both: Resource is useful for both teachers and students
_badges.Interactive: Resource is a game, quiz, or interactive tool
_badges.Login Required: An account or login is needed to access the resource
_badges.Teacher Resource: Use on Books section items — teacher-facing reference material

links.title: Teach with ICT
links.description: Strategies and resources for teaching ICT and Computer Science.

links.title: Computer Science Circles
links.description: University of Waterloo introduction to CS and Python. Free to use — login available to save progress.

links.title: Teckno CS Course
links.description: Free Computer Science and coding courses from Dell, aimed at Leaving Certificate CS students.

links.title: Thonny
links.description: A beginner-friendly Python IDE with a built-in debugger. Free to download. Ideal for students writing their first Python programs.

links.title: Visual Studio Code
links.description: A powerful, free code editor from Microsoft supporting Python, JavaScript, and many other languages via extensions.

links.title: GitHub Desktop
links.description: A GUI client for cloning and managing Git repositories from GitHub without using the command line.

links.title: VS Codium
links.description: An open-source version of VS Code with Microsoft telemetry removed. Identical in features but fully open-source.

links.title: Replit
links.description: Browser-based IDE supporting many languages including Python. Free tier available but has limitations on usage.

links.title: Google Colab
links.description: A free, cloud-based Jupyter notebook environment from Google. Good for Python and data analysis work. Requires a Google account.

links.title: Trinket.io
links.description: A simple browser-based Python editor — no login needed for basic use. Note: the free version is limited to Python 2.

links.title: VSCode Dev
links.description: VS Code running in the browser. Opens GitHub repos directly — useful when students cannot install software on school devices.

links.title: Codepad
links.description: A browser-based code editor similar to Replit and Trinket, with more flexibility than Trinket. Currently free to use.

links.title: Turing Labs (Amazon Future Engineer)
links.description: Structured Python learning from Amazon Future Engineer. Suitable for students beginning to develop their Python skills.

links.title: Python Cheatsheet
links.description: A concise reference covering Python syntax, data types, loops, functions, and more. Best for students who already know the basics and need a quick lookup.

links.title: Network Animations
links.description: Animated explanations of how networks operate. Useful as a visual aid when introducing networking concepts at LC level.

links.title: Network Protocol Matching Quiz
links.description: A Wordwall word-matching quiz on network protocols. Works well as a classroom starter or homework task for the LC networking topic.

links.title: Network Hardware Word Match Quiz
links.description: A Wordwall word-match quiz on network hardware. Works well as a classroom starter or homework task for the LC networking topic.

links.title: Network Design Drag and Drop
links.description: A drag-and-drop activity for identifying and placing common network hardware components. Good for consolidating LC networking content.

links.title: ChatGPT Prompting Cheatsheet
links.description: A concise reference for writing effective prompts for ChatGPT and other large language models.

links.title: Black Box AI Explainer (TechTarget)
links.description: A clear explanation of what black box AI is and how it works. Relevant to the LC AI strand.

links.title: Our World in Data
links.description: Free, open-access datasets and visualisations on global topics — health, education, climate, and more. No login required. A strong starting point for ALT2 data projects.

links.title: Statista
links.description: A large statistics and market data platform. Some data is freely accessible. Useful for finding ready-made datasets for ALT2.

links.title: Kaggle
links.description: A large library of free, open datasets across many topics. No login required to browse. Good for ALT2 — guide students to pick smaller, well-structured datasets.

links.title: Logicly
links.description: A drag-and-drop logic gate simulator with a free trial available in-browser. Well suited to quick classroom demonstrations of AND, OR, NOT, and compound gates.

links.title: Logic Circuit
links.description: Free downloadable software for building logic circuits and generating truth tables automatically. Useful for checking student work.

links.title: EveryCircuit
links.description: An online circuit simulator that includes logic gates alongside broader electronics components. More expansive than Logicly.

links.title: OS Definitions Quiz
links.description: A Wordwall activity matching operating system terms to their definitions. Works well as a classroom starter for the OS topic.

links.title: OnWorks — Virtual Machines Online
links.description: Run Windows, Mac, or Linux in a virtual machine in the browser — no installation needed. A practical classroom tool for demonstrating different OS environments.

links.title: PCjs Machines
links.description: Emulates vintage computers running old operating systems in the browser. Good for showing students OS history and how much interfaces have changed.

links.title: WebOS.js
links.description: Run versions of operating systems including Mac OS in the browser. More of a curiosity link — useful for illustrating OS history.

links.title: WinWorld OS Library
links.description: A library of disk images for vintage operating systems — useful for demonstrating OS evolution in class rather than as a practical tool.

links.title: Micro:bit and AI
links.description: Explore AI and machine learning through movement using the Micro:bit. Requires a physical Micro:bit device.

links.title: Computational Thinking Guide
links.description: An overview of what computational thinking is and how to teach it. Teacher-facing background reading.

links.title: Logic Puzzles (Puzzle Baron)
links.description: Free logic grid puzzles that develop logical reasoning skills. Can be shared directly with students as a starter or extension task.

links.title: CS Planning Tool (National Workshop 7)
links.description: A curriculum planning spreadsheet from LC CS National Workshop 7. Teacher-facing — check if still current before sharing.

links.title: Code Puzzle
links.description: Create Parsons-style puzzles from code — students put lines in the correct order. Good for consolidation activities.

links.title: Code Puzzle — Example
links.description: A ready-made Code Puzzle example — put the code in the correct order. Useful to show students how the tool works.

links.title: Deck of Cards
links.description: A virtual deck of cards for demonstrating sorting methods in class. Works well alongside a sorting algorithms explanation.

links.title: Sorting Algorithms Visualiser (Toptal)
links.description: Animates common sorting algorithms side by side. Great as a classroom demo — students can see the difference between algorithms visually.

links.title: Flippy Bit and the Attack of the Hexadecimals
links.description: A browser game that teaches hexadecimal conversion. A fun consolidation activity after introducing binary and hex.

links.title: Nearpod Library
links.description: Interactive presentations for the classroom including quizzes and polls. Free tier available. Useful for formative assessment across CS topics.

links.title: Logic Puzzles (Puzzle Baron)
links.description: Logic grid puzzles — good for developing logical reasoning. Works well as a starter or extension task for early finishers.

links.title: Awesome Python
links.description: A curated list of Python frameworks, libraries, and resources. More useful for teachers and advanced LC students — the breadth can be overwhelming for beginners.

links.title: JavaScript30
links.description: A 30-day JavaScript challenge — 30 apps in 30 days with no frameworks or libraries. Good for LC students who want to build real things with JavaScript.

links.title: The Algorithms
links.description: Data structures and algorithms implemented in many languages. Useful for teachers preparing content and for strong LC students studying implementations.

links.title: The Odin Project
links.description: An open-source full-stack web development curriculum. Suitable for motivated LC students who want a structured self-study path beyond the classroom.

links.title: Build Your Own X
links.description: Step-by-step guides to recreating technologies from scratch — databases, shells, web servers, and more. Primarily teacher-level but inspiring for advanced LC students.

links.title: JavaScript Questions
links.description: A long list of advanced JavaScript questions with clear explanations. Good for LC students consolidating their JavaScript knowledge.

links.title: OSSU Computer Science
links.description: A roadmap to a full CS education using free online resources. Primarily teacher-facing — useful for understanding the broader CS landscape beyond the LC course.

links.title: Corey Schafer
links.description: High-quality coding tutorials covering Python, Django, Git, and more. Clear and well-paced — suited to LC students who want in-depth explanations.

links.title: Daniel Murray Makes
links.description: A CS teacher from Dublin covering topics relevant to the Irish LC CS course. Worth sharing directly with students.

links.title: 100 Ideas for Secondary Teachers: Outstanding Computing Lessons
links.description: A practical book of 100 ready-to-use ideas for teaching computing at secondary level. Published by Bloomsbury.
